title: Kinesis Data Streams & Amazon Data Firehose
summary: Real-time stream ingestion, fan-out to consumers, and managed delivery into S3, Redshift and more.
services: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
tldr: **Kinesis Data Streams (KDS)** is a durable, replayable stream: many consumers each read every record, in order per partition key, with sub-second latency and retention up to 365 days.

**Amazon Data Firehose** (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) is zero-administration *delivery*: it buffers, converts (JSON to Parquet/ORC), partitions and loads data into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, Iceberg tables or HTTP endpoints. Near real-time, no replay, no custom consumers.
Throttling (`ProvisionedThroughputExceededException`) means a **hot shard** or too little capacity: fix the partition key, add shards, or switch to **on-demand** mode.
Need windowed analytics or stateful processing on the stream? Use **Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink**.

keyFacts.text: Write limit **per shard** in provisioned mode. Shared read is 2 MB/s per shard across all standard (polling) consumers.
**Enhanced fan-out** gives each registered consumer its own 2 MB/s per shard, pushed over HTTP/2 (`SubscribeToShard`) with lower latency.
Default KDS retention is 24 hours and can be extended up to 365 days, so consumers can **reprocess** history after a bug fix.
Lets a Lambda event source mapping process up to 10 batches per shard at once while keeping order **per partition key**.
KDS scales shard capacity automatically for unpredictable traffic; no shard planning. Consumers keep using the same APIs unchanged.

traps: Enhanced fan-out fixes **read** contention only. It does nothing for producer write throttling.
Increasing retention never fixes throttling; it only lets consumers go further back in time.
Adding shards does not help if the partition key is low-cardinality (country, region); all hot traffic still hashes to one shard.
Firehose cannot be read by several custom consumers or replayed, so it is wrong when apps need every record with sub-second latency.
A bad record on a Lambda stream consumer blocks the shard; use `BisectBatchOnFunctionError`, `MaximumRetryAttempts` and an on-failure destination, not an async DLQ.

sections.heading: Fixing producer throttling, in order
sections.body:
1. **Check the partition key.** Low cardinality creates hot shards; switch to device, user or session ID.
2. **Batch tiny records.** Use the KPL to aggregate many small records into one Kinesis record, which avoids the 1,000 records/s limit.
3. **Add capacity.** `UpdateShardCount` (or split hot shards) in provisioned mode, or move to **on-demand** mode when traffic is spiky and you don't want to plan shards.
